findings.title: Red does not print the tail of its output (FR-7, CT-3)
quotes: On acceptance red prints, after `frozen:`, `output:` and "the last 20 lines of its output" (FR-7), each indented two spaces.
findings.fix: print `output:` and the last 20 lines, each indented two spaces, and add the test.

sources.situation: red is accepted, and the output ends after the `frozen:` list with no `output:` section. The code at `src/nio/implement.py:549` returns only `"red: {tid} accepted", "frozen:"` plus the frozen files.

findings.reason: Red's `output:` tail is FR-7/AC-8/TC-8, which tasks.md assigns to T-6 in E-3 (T-6 "Red prints its last 20 output lines", Depends on T-4). T-4 in E-2 serves only AC-1 to AC-6, so `implement.py:549` not printing it is not a gap in this gate's epic.

findings.title: Tests named for AC-7 to AC-10 do not exist
findings.fix: write those tests, or move the ACs to the epic that implements them.

sources.situation: the pack lists `test_ac7_worker_card_scopes_its_tests`, `test_ac8_red_prints_its_tail`, `test_ac9_evidence_reads_self_check_lines` and `test_ac10_crashed_file_is_failed`, all at line 0. The journey run printed "no test named" for AC-9 and AC-10 and "ran 0 tests, 0 failed". Nothing proves the worker-card scoping, the red tail, or evidence reading of self-check lines. The crashed-suite behaviour is covered only by `test_review_fails_a_crashed_self_check_suite` (`tests/test_implement.py:1720`), which sits in the attacks list and was not run. If these ACs belong to E-2, they are missing evidence.

In the epic-closing suite, file A has a pre-existing FAIL line that is in the baseline's `failing`. File B crashes before printing its lines, which is the case CT-3 says to fail. `r["failing"]` is non-empty, so the new branch is skipped. `new` is empty because the FAIL is in the baseline, so `reasons` stays empty and the review passes with a crashed file.

findings.reason: The first situation (no tests for AC-7 to AC-10) is out of E-2. tasks.md puts them in T-5, T-6 (E-3) and T-7 (E-4), so that part is refuted. The correctness situation holds. `implement.py:585` fails a crash only when `not r["failing"]`, and CT-3 words the rule the same way ("`failing` is empty"). A crashed file B next to a baseline-failing file A leaves `failing` non-empty and `new` empty, so review passes. The `collected < baseline` check at line 594 catches it only on a full run, not on the `quick` epic suite (line 580).

findings.title: No per-test pass evidence for AC-1 to AC-6
quotes: Per-test results are unknown: the suite's runner can't be read per test; the exit code and output are in `suite`.
findings.fix: run the suite fresh at this gate, or run the TCs that cover these tests.

sources.situation: the suite pass is reused from T-4's review, and the misuse tests were not run. The bodies of the AC-4, AC-5 and AC-6 tests do exercise the criteria: the history line and command, the "no tests ran" refusal, and the check that no other suite command ran. A pass of the tests themselves is still unconfirmed.

findings.title: The self-check runner entry has no match key the contract names
findings.fix: either add `"match": r"(?!)"` to the entry, or change CT-7 to say the key is absent. The code comment already records the choice.

sources.situation: CT-7 gives the entry a `match` key that matches nothing. The diff omits it and relies on `r.get("match", r"(?!)")` in `runner`. Behaviour is the same, but the code and the contract disagree on the shape that `wrong_reason` and later readers rely on.

CT-7 anchors the line with `$`. The code matches `r"^ran \d+ tests?, \d+ failed"` with no `$`. A line such as `ran 1 tests, 0 failed ...` is therefore read as self-check. This is only a looseness, but code and spec differ.

findings.title: The self-check detection regex has no end anchor
findings.fix: add `$` to the code regex, or drop the `$` from CT-7. The code is the simpler fix and matches CT-7 as written.

sources.situation: CT-7 wants a line that ends after `failed`. The code also accepts a line such as `ran 1 tests, 0 failed (see log)`, so a non-self-check output with that line is read as `self-check`. Red then applies the self-check rules to it, and FR-2 is not the only source of such a line.

findings.title: Red's "no tests ran" check matches the line anywhere, not where FR-4 says
quotes: IF a red command's output ends its run with `ran 0 tests`
`none = any(m in out for m in RUNNERS.get(name, {}).get("none", []))`
findings.fix: check only the last `ran` line of the output for the self-check runner, or amend FR-4 and the table to say "contains". Keep the other runners as they are, as the existing convention.

sources.situation: FR-4 refuses red only when the run ends with `ran 0 tests`. The code refuses it when that text appears anywhere in the output. A failing test that prints an earlier `ran 0 tests` line, then ends with `ran 1 tests, 0 failed`, would be refused as "no tests ran" when a test did run and fail. I did not see such output in the pack, so this is inferred.

findings.title: An import or syntax crash in the test file is accepted as a valid red
findings.fix: Either refuse red when the code is non-zero and there is a Traceback but no `ran` line, or accept this as the FR-9 unknown-runner behaviour and say so in the spec.

sources.situation: A scoped red command crashes at import, for example a missing module or a syntax error. The script prints a Traceback and no `ran N tests` line. `runner(command, out)` returns None, because the command's own words don't match and the output has no summary line. `wrong_reason(None, ...)` returns "", so red is accepted (`code != 0`). The red failure is for the wrong reason, which red is meant to refuse. Because `error` is empty, self-check has no way to flag it even when it is recognised.
